facts.f: The CPU is the 'brain' of a computer.
facts.e: CPU stands for Central Processing Unit. It carries out the instructions of programs.

facts.f: RAM is a computer's short-term working memory.
facts.e: Whatever is in RAM is lost when the power is switched off. Files are saved on storage instead.

facts.f: Computers store everything as 0s and 1s.
facts.e: This is called binary. Every photo, song and game is made of long strings of 0s and 1s.

facts.f: One byte is made of 8 bits.
facts.e: A bit is a single 0 or 1. One byte can store a single letter, like 'A'.

facts.f: Charles Babbage is called the 'father of the computer'.
facts.e: In the 1830s he designed the Analytical Engine, a mechanical computer.

facts.f: Ada Lovelace is often called the first computer programmer.
facts.e: In 1843 she published steps for Babbage's Analytical Engine to calculate a series of numbers.

facts.f: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989.
facts.e: He made web pages that could link to each other.

facts.f: The internet and the World Wide Web are not the same thing.
facts.e: The internet is the giant network of connected computers. The web is the pages and sites we visit using it.

facts.f: A URL is the address of a web page.
facts.e: URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator.

facts.f: The 'S' in HTTPS stands for secure.
facts.e: It means the information between your device and the website is scrambled so others cannot read it.

facts.f: A strong password is long and hard to guess.
facts.e: Mix words, numbers and symbols, and never share your password with friends.

facts.f: Never share personal details like your address, school or phone number with strangers online.
facts.e: If someone online makes you uncomfortable, tell a trusted adult.

facts.f: Phishing is a trick where fake messages try to steal your passwords.
facts.e: Do not click on strange links or share OTPs, even if the message looks official.

facts.f: A computer virus is a harmful program that can copy itself.
facts.e: Antivirus software and careful downloading help keep computers safe.

facts.f: Keyboards and mice are input devices. Monitors and printers are output devices.
facts.e: Input devices put information in; output devices show or give results out.

facts.f: The QWERTY keyboard is named after the first six letters on its top letter row.
facts.e: This layout was first designed for typewriters in the 1870s.

facts.f: GPS finds your location using signals from satellites.
facts.e: Your phone works out where it is by timing signals from several satellites.

facts.f: India has its own satellite navigation system called NavIC.
facts.e: It was built by ISRO to give accurate positions over India and nearby regions.

facts.f: Wi-Fi uses radio waves to connect devices without wires.
facts.e: A router sends and receives these waves.

facts.f: A pixel is a tiny dot of colour on a screen.
facts.e: A screen picture is made of millions of pixels.

facts.f: Screens make all their colours by mixing red, green and blue light.
facts.e: Each pixel has tiny red, green and blue parts. Mixing them in different amounts gives every colour.

facts.f: Artificial intelligence (AI) lets computers learn from examples.
facts.e: AI is used for things like recognising speech and translating languages, but it can still make mistakes.

facts.f: An algorithm is a step-by-step set of instructions to solve a problem.
facts.e: A recipe is like an algorithm for cooking.

facts.f: A mistake in a computer program is called a bug.
facts.e: In 1947, Grace Hopper's team found a real moth stuck inside a computer and taped it into their logbook.

facts.f: Early electronic computers in the 1940s filled whole rooms.
facts.e: ENIAC, one of the first, weighed about 27 tonnes.

facts.f: UPI lets people in India send money instantly using a mobile phone.
facts.e: It was launched in 2016 by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).

facts.f: The word 'robot' comes from a Czech play written in 1920.
facts.e: Karel Čapek's play R.U.R. used it, from a Czech word meaning forced work.

facts.f: In binary, the number 10 means two.
facts.e: Binary has only two digits, 0 and 1. Each place is worth twice the place to its right.

facts.f: The computers that guided the Apollo spacecraft to the Moon were far less powerful than a modern smartphone.
facts.e: Technology has improved enormously in a few decades.

facts.f: Bluetooth is named after a Viking-era king of Denmark, Harald Bluetooth.
facts.e: He was known for uniting tribes, just as Bluetooth connects devices.

facts.f: Ray Tomlinson sent the first email between two computers on a network in 1971.
facts.e: He chose the @ symbol to separate the user's name from the computer's name.

facts.f: Cloud storage means your files are kept on other computers over the internet.
facts.e: These computers, called servers, are in big buildings called data centres.

facts.f: On most computers, Ctrl + Z undoes your last action.
facts.e: Ctrl + C copies and Ctrl + V pastes.

facts.f: Scratch is a block-based coding language made at MIT for young learners.
facts.e: You snap blocks together like puzzle pieces to make games and stories.

facts.f: Most phone touchscreens sense the tiny electric charge in your finger.
facts.e: That is why they usually do not work with a gloved hand.

facts.f: The QR code was invented in Japan in 1994.
facts.e: It was first used to track car parts in factories.

facts.f: A search engine finds web pages using a giant index.
facts.e: Programs called crawlers visit pages and note what is on them.

facts.f: If someone bullies you online, do not reply. Save the messages and tell a trusted adult.
facts.e: Blocking and reporting the bully also helps.

facts.f: PARAM 8000, built by C-DAC in 1991, is often called India's first supercomputer.
facts.e: Indian scientists built it themselves after the USA refused to sell India a supercomputer.

facts.f: Two-step verification adds an extra code to protect your account.
facts.e: Even if someone learns your password, they also need the code.

facts.f: Fibre-optic cables carry data as flashes of light through thin glass threads.
facts.e: They can carry huge amounts of data very quickly.

facts.f: Most internet traffic between continents travels through cables on the sea floor.
facts.e: Not through satellites, as many people think.

quiz.q: What does CPU stand for?
quiz.x: The CPU carries out a computer's instructions.

quiz.q: How do computers store information?
quiz.x: Everything in a computer is stored in binary.

quiz.q: How many bits make one byte?
quiz.x: 8 bits = 1 byte.

quiz.q: Who invented the World Wide Web?
quiz.x: Tim Berners-Lee invented the web in 1989.

quiz.q: Who is often called the first computer programmer?
quiz.x: Ada Lovelace wrote steps for Babbage's Analytical Engine in 1843.

quiz.q: Who is called the 'father of the computer'?
quiz.x: Babbage designed the Analytical Engine in the 1830s.

quiz.q: Which of these is an input device?
quiz.x: A keyboard puts information into the computer.

quiz.q: What does the 'S' in HTTPS stand for?
quiz.x: HTTPS means the connection is encrypted.

quiz.q: What do we call fake messages that try to steal passwords?
quiz.x: Phishing messages pretend to be someone you trust.

quiz.q: What is India's own satellite navigation system called?
quiz.x: NavIC was built by ISRO. GPS is American.

quiz.q: What is a step-by-step set of instructions to solve a problem called?
quiz.x: Algorithms are like recipes for computers.

quiz.q: What is the binary number 101 in our usual numbers?
quiz.x: 101 = 1 four + 0 twos + 1 one = 5.

quiz.q: What is a tiny dot of colour on a screen called?
quiz.x: Screens are made of millions of pixels.

quiz.q: Which three colours of light do screens mix to make all colours?
quiz.x: Screens use RGB light. Red, yellow and blue are the traditional colours for mixing paint.

quiz.q: Bluetooth is named after...
o: The colour of the first chip
quiz.x: Harald Bluetooth united tribes, and Bluetooth unites devices.

quiz.q: Who chose the @ symbol for email addresses?
quiz.x: He sent the first networked email in 1971.

quiz.q: What should you do if someone bullies you online?
o: Don't reply, save it and tell a trusted adult
quiz.x: Trusted adults can help you block, report and stop the bullying.

quiz.q: Where was the Scratch coding language made?
quiz.x: Scratch was made at MIT for young learners.

quiz.q: Which machine, built by C-DAC in 1991, is often called India's first supercomputer?
quiz.x: C-DAC built PARAM 8000 in 1991.

quiz.q: What does Ctrl + Z usually do?
quiz.x: Ctrl + Z undoes your last action.

quiz.q: The word 'robot' first appeared in a play from which country?
quiz.x: Karel Čapek's 1920 play R.U.R. introduced the word.
